system_overview: This specification models an asynchronous non-blocking atomic commitment algorithm with failure detectors, based on Guerraoui's 2001 paper on the hardness of failure-sensitive agreement problems. The protocol allows N processes to vote YES or NO and reach a consistent commit or abort decision. It uses a threshold-based counting abstraction rather than explicit message sets: instead of tracking individual messages, it counts how many YES and NO messages have been sent and received. Processes may crash, and a failure detector reports suspected crashes.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N processes (numbered 1 through N). Each process votes, sends its vote, receives vote counts, and decides to commit or abort. A failure detector provides each process with a boolean indicating whether it suspects some process has crashed. Crashed processes (marked with a special status) no longer participate but their unsent votes contribute to upper bounds on possible messages.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) The total count of NO messages sent by correct (non-crashed) processes. (2) The total count of YES messages sent by correct processes. (3) An upper bound on the number of NO messages that crashed processes might have sent (incremented when a process that voted NO crashes before sending). (4) An upper bound on the number of YES messages that crashed processes might have sent (incremented when a process that voted YES crashes before sending). (5) For each process, the count of YES messages it has received so far. (6) For each process, the count of NO messages it has received so far. (7) A failure detector output for each process (boolean). (8) A program counter for each process indicating its state: voting YES, voting NO, vote sent, decided abort, decided commit, or crashed.
initial_state: No messages have been sent or received (all counters are zero). Each process starts with a nondeterministic initial vote of YES or NO. The failure detector output is nondeterministically initialized for each process.
actions: Process actions: (1) Crash: A non-crashed process crashes. If it had not yet sent its vote, the upper bound for its vote type (YES or NO) is incremented, accounting for the possibility that it might have sent before crashing. (2) Receive: A process that has sent its vote can receive one message at a time. If its received YES count is below the sum of sent YES messages plus the upper bound from crashed processes, it can receive one more YES. Similarly for NO. If all available messages have been received, the process does nothing (to avoid deadlock). (3) Send YES: A process whose vote is YES and whose failure detector does not suspect a crash sends its vote (incrementing the sent YES count) and transitions to the sent state. (4) Send NO: Same as send YES but for NO votes. (5) Abort before sending: If a process's failure detector suspects a crash and the process has not yet sent its vote (still in YES or NO state), it immediately aborts. (6) Abort after sending: If a process has sent its vote and has received at least one NO message, it aborts. (7) Commit: If a process has sent its vote, has received zero NO messages, and has received at least N YES messages, it commits. (8) Do nothing: An unchanged-variables transition to prevent deadlock after deciding.
safety_properties: Agreement: No two correct processes decide differently -- it is impossible for one to commit while another aborts. Abort validity: If some process votes NO, then no process ever commits. Commit validity: If all processes vote YES and no failure is suspected, then no process crashes or aborts. Type invariant: All counters are in valid ranges (0 to N), received counts are bounded by sent counts plus upper bounds, program counters are in valid states, and failure detector outputs are booleans.
liveness_properties: Termination: If no process ever crashes and no process is ever suspected by the failure detector, then eventually every process reaches a decision (commit or abort).
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the combined receive, send, abort, and commit actions, ensuring non-crashed processes eventually make progress. Crash transitions and the do-nothing transition are not subject to fairness. The specification also defines two alternative initial conditions: one where all processes vote YES and one where all processes vote NO, each with its own specification formula. The failure detector satisfies two properties: every faulty process is permanently suspected, and no process is suspected unless it actually crashes. The counting abstraction makes the state space finite without requiring explicit message tracking.
